models.label: ECMWF IFS 0.25°
models.note: ECMWF's operational physics model, open-data release. Its gust field is a maximum over the output interval, not an instantaneous value, so gust factors look large in light air.

models.label: ECMWF AIFS
models.note: ECMWF's machine-learning model - a genuinely independent opinion. Publishes no gust field, so gusts come from IFS and ICON-2i only.

models.label: ItaliaMeteo ICON-2i
models.note: ItaliaMeteo / ARPAE high-resolution model for Italy - the finest grid available here. Runs only ~60-72 h ahead and updates every 12 h, so it drops out of the longer-range view.

models.label: Météo-France MFWAM
models.note: Full sea-state decomposition - total wave, wind wave and swell with heights, directions and periods.

models.label: ECMWF WAM 0.25°
models.note: Total significant wave height only - used to cross-check MFWAM.

briefing.headline: Light and benign: under 8 kt at Salina tonight, with a calm 06:00 window for the 24 nm hop to Portorosa.
briefing.synopsis: The payload carries no surface pressure analysis, so I can't describe the synoptic pattern directly - what the models show is a light, slack airflow with no organised gradient. Across the islands today the breeze has been ESE at 5-10 kt (Salina 7.5 kt ESE at 18:00, ECMWF IFS/AIFS/ICON-2i consensus, runs 08 Oct 00Z/06Z), backing SSW overnight and swinging through NW to N by late morning tomorrow. Everything stays Beaufort 2-3 through tomorrow; the only growth is in the sea state, with Salina waves building from 0.7 ft tonight to about 2.0 ft by Friday evening and 2.4 ft on Saturday midday. Models diverge sharply on tomorrow's afternoon wind speed - see the confidence note.
briefing.overnight_anchorage: Porto Santa Marina Salina is the recommendation and the choice doesn't much matter tonight: both it and Rinella score as sheltered. Consensus at Santa Marina is 5.6 kt SSW gusting 19.0 kt with 0.5 ft of SSW swell - the berth is open to the SSW sector (150-210°) but there is nothing in that direction to work with. Overnight at Salina the consensus runs 5.6 kt SSW at midnight easing to 4.0 kt NW by 06:00, waves 0.7-0.8 ft. Only a real build in SSW swell would argue for shifting to Rinella, and nothing in this payload shows one.
briefing.tomorrow_morning: 06:00 is the recommended departure for Salina → Portorosa, 24 nm on 156°T. The 06:00-10:00 window shows 4.0 kt WSW, 0.8 ft seas, beam reach at 96° TWA - almost certainly a motor-sail. Conditions are flagged as deteriorating after 09:00, though only in the modest sense that wind backs N then NE and seas build to 1.1-1.9 ft by the afternoon windows; all five windows out to a 14:00 departure are computed 'go'. Note those are conservative threshold calculations, not a decision - the call is yours.

passage_notes.note: Completed conditions were benign throughout: 5-7 kt ESE/SE, seas 0.6-0.8 ft, mostly head to wind and motoring.

Best at 06:00: 4.0 kt WSW, 0.8 ft, beam reach. By 12:00 departure it is 7.5 kt NE, 1.7 ft, broad reach; by 14:00, 7.2 kt ESE, 1.9 ft, close hauled. All windows computed 'go'. Arrival berth Portorosa Marina is fully enclosed, 4.4 kt SSE with 1.2 ft WNW swell outside.

cautions: Gust figures look wild against the means - 26-31 kt gusts over a 4-8 kt mean in tomorrow's windows, and 41.4 kt at Filicudi midday Friday. These are interval-maximum values from the IFS/ICON-2i gust field in light air, reported but not treated as a caution by the thresholds. Don't ignore them entirely in a squally sea breeze, but don't plan around them either.

Models disagree materially on tomorrow afternoon: Salina 12:00 spans 1.4-13.0 kt and 18:00 spans 1.8-16.7 kt; Lipari 18:00 spans 2.1-22.7 kt. An early start removes that uncertainty from the equation.

Sea state is building behind the front end of the forecast - Salina waves reach 2.0 ft Friday evening and 2.4 ft Saturday midday, Filicudi 2.6 ft. Relevant if anyone is thinking about an island hop rather than running straight to Portorosa.
briefing.confidence_note: Short-range agreement is good (12-24 h mean wind shift 0.9 kt, max 3.0 kt over the last five runs), but the models split by more than 6 kt on tomorrow afternoon's wind at Salina, Lipari and Panarea, and direction in air this light is inherently loose (mean 22° shift at 12-24 h).
